headline: High: xonsh can read/write and execute shell by default, while python-cheatsheet is documentation-only, creating a dangerous asymmetry for leakage and cascading misuse if paired through shared files or copied output.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and has no I/O surfaces, so it cannot directly inject xonsh. The only plausible bridge is manual copy-paste or external file transfer into xonsh, which can parse shell text. That makes injection possible but not default, and the blast radius is limited to the operator’s session.
conditions: IF the operator copies content from python-cheatsheet into xonsh as shell input, THEN prompt-like text can influence execution.
IF xonsh is used to source or eval copied snippets, THEN injected commands can run.
mitigations: Keep python-cheatsheet output as plain text, not shell input.
Require a human review step before pasting into xonsh.
Use a separate scratch buffer for copied snippets.
Disable eval/source patterns in xonsh workflows.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for pasted content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: python-cheatsheet touches no data classes, but xonsh reads and writes filesystem contents and environment variables by default. If the pair shares a workspace, xonsh can expose local files or env data through copied outputs or logs. The interaction is plausible from the profiles alone, though not directly documented.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same workspace, THEN xonsh can read files that python-cheatsheet references or generates.
IF xonsh prints file or environment contents into shared outputs, THEN those contents can leak beyond the intended scope.
mitigations: Run xonsh in a separate directory from documentation artifacts.
Avoid placing secrets in any shared workspace.
Review xonsh commands before execution.
Redirect sensitive command output away from shared logs.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation between the agents.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: python-cheatsheet has no write or execution capabilities, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. xonsh can write files and run shell commands, but without a second writer there is no meaningful conflict pathway. The pair therefore has only a small residual risk if the operator manually edits the same files.
conditions: IF the operator manually edits the same file from both workflows, THEN xonsh writes can overwrite documentation changes.
IF a shared directory is used for generated artifacts, THEN xonsh may clobber files created around python-cheatsheet content.
mitigations: Use separate directories for docs and execution artifacts.
Back up files before running xonsh writes.
Avoid concurrent manual edits to the same file.
Check diffs before saving changes.
requires-engineering: add file locking for shared outputs.

D_cascading_error.rationale: python-cheatsheet can supply reference text that xonsh may treat as actionable shell content if copied or scripted. Because xonsh has execution authority, an unverified snippet can cascade into real commands. The pair lacks built-in verification or provenance controls, so the risk is present in ordinary workflows.
conditions: IF xonsh consumes text copied from python-cheatsheet as commands, THEN incorrect or malicious instructions can execute.
IF the operator uses python-cheatsheet examples without validation, THEN xonsh may perform unintended actions.
mitigations: Verify snippets before running them in xonsh.
Use dry-run or echo-only checks first.
Keep a manual approval step for any command derived from documentation.
Limit xonsh sessions to non-sensitive tasks.
requires-engineering: add command allowlisting or linting.

E_compliance.rationale: No sensitive data class, residency, or regulated workload is identified for python-cheatsheet, and xonsh’s profile does not request special scopes or handle regulated data by default. The main compliance issue is operational hygiene around local files, which is a small gap rather than a breach pathway.
conditions: IF regulated data is manually placed into xonsh’s workspace, THEN local handling policies may apply.
IF the operator stores compliance-sensitive artifacts in shared files, THEN retention controls must be enforced.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace.
Document local retention rules for generated files.
Use separate folders for sensitive and non-sensitive work.
Review any logs before sharing them.
requires-engineering: add policy-based data classification controls.
